key_insight: Conformal Policy Control uses conformal calibration on data from a safe reference policy to build a probabilistic regulator that limits how much a new (optimized) policy can deviate, giving finite-sample coverage guarantees while avoiding excessive conservatism.
problem_solved: Balances the need for exploration/improvement with safety in high-stakes settings by preventing catastrophic behavioral deviations from a trusted policy without forcing overly conservative imitation.
method: Treat a trusted safe policy as a reference and collect its trajectories / conformity scores.
Apply conformal calibration to those scores to compute acceptance thresholds that guarantee a desired probabilistic bound on allowable deviation.

At deployment, run the candidate policy through the calibrated test: if it passes, allow its actions; if it fails, fall back to the safe policy (probabilistic regulator). Compatible with any optimized/unseen policy.
impact: Gives practitioners a practical, distribution-free tool to deploy exploratory policies with explicit finite-sample safety guarantees, enabling more effective and principled exploration in real-world, high-risk domains.
visual_elements: Flowchart: Candidate policy -> conformal test -> Accept (deploy) / Reject (fallback to safe policy)
Calibration plot showing conformity-score distribution and chosen threshold with empirical coverage
Tradeoff curve: exploration benefit vs. violation risk demonstrating reduced conservatism at fixed safety level
Trajectory heatmap or timeline marking points where regulator triggered fallback to the safe policy
paper_authors: Drew Prinster, Clara Fannjiang, Ji Won Park, Kyunghyun Cho, Anqi Liu
